Get Properties at Fractional Costs at Fayette County, Pennsylvania Tax Deed Sale

If you’re looking for investment opportunities in Fayette County, Pennsylvania, tax sales can be a great way to acquire properties at significantly reduced prices. Here’s everything you need to know to get started:

Fayette County Tax Lien Information Links

  • Fayette County Tax Sales: Upset, Repository, Judicial Sales
  • Tax Claim Bureau: Fayette County Tax Claim Bureau
  • County Website: Fayette County, PA
  • Auction Site: 2 West Main Street, Uniontown, PA 15401, in the Meeting Room on the 1st Floor

Understanding Tax Sales in Fayette County

Upset Sale:

  • When: Annually between the 2nd Monday and the last day of September.
  • Details: Properties sold with existing liens and judgments. Any unsold properties may advance to the Judicial Sale.
  • Registration: You must pre-register with the Fayette County Tax Claim Bureau. We recommend conducting a title search.
  • Payment: Cash, money order, certified check, or official check (no out-of-state checks).

Judicial (Free & Clear) Sale:

  • Details: Properties sold free of most liens and judgments unless not served by the Fayette County sheriff’s department.
  • Registration: Pre-registration is required.
  • Payment: Same as Upset Sale, no credit or debit cards accepted.

Repository Sale:

  • Details: The Fayette County Tax Claim Bureau lists properties not sold at the Judicial Sale here, selling them free of all tax and municipal claims, mortgages, and liens, except for ground rents and possible IRS liens.

Pro Tips

  • Research: Always conduct a thorough title search and understand any existing liens or judgments.
  • Pre-Register: Ensure you pre-register for the sales. Registration for the Free & Clear Sale is open now.
  • Payment: Be prepared with the accepted forms of payment.
  • Due Diligence: Investigate the condition of the property and any potential possession issues.

Fayette County Tax Sale FAQs

What is the Upset Sale?
The Upset Sale is an annual auction where properties are sold with all existing liens and judgments. It usually takes place between the second Monday and the last day of September.

How can I participate in the Judicial Sale?
To participate in the Judicial Sale, you must pre-register with the Tax Claim Bureau and prepare to pay with cash, money order, certified check, or personal checks with a bank letter.

What happens if I don’t get a property in the Upset or Judicial Sales?
Properties that don’t sell in these sales move to the Repository Sale, where the county sells them free of most claims and liens.

Where can I get more information?
You can visit the Fayette County Tax Claim Bureau’s official page for detailed information and updates on tax sales.
